title: Ward 04, Parkdale–High Park: multiplexes, before you vote

sections.heading: What may fit
sections.template_text: In this ward, {{could_lots}} house lots may fit at least one of the City's four free multiplex designs. That is {{could_pct}}% of house lots. This count is an upper bound: it shows where a design may fit, not what gets built.
sections.text: In this ward, 3,900 house lots may fit at least one of the City's four free multiplex designs. That is 32.5% of house lots. This count is an upper bound: it shows where a design may fit, not what gets built.

sections.heading: Why lots don't fit
sections.template_text: The most common reason is that the house is attached: {{top_rule_count}} lots are semis or row houses. In all, {{attached_pct}}% of house lots are attached, and the City's free designs are for detached lots.
sections.text: The most common reason is that the house is attached: 4,300 lots are semis or row houses. In all, 35.8% of house lots are attached, and the City's free designs are for detached lots.

sections.heading: Multiplex permits issued
sections.template_text: Since May 2023, {{did_permits}} multiplex permits have been issued in this ward, before the free designs existed. That is about one permit for every {{lots_per_permit}} lots where a design may fit.
sections.text: Since May 2023, 41 multiplex permits have been issued in this ward, before the free designs existed. That is about one permit for every 95 lots where a design may fit.

sections.heading: What isn't checked
sections.template_text: Suplex did not check {{not_checked_lots}} lots: condos, lots outside the residential house zones, lots under an older bylaw, larger buildings and lots too irregular to measure. It also does not check heritage rules, trees, sewers or site-specific exceptions. This is a screening, not a permit or legal advice.
sections.text: Suplex did not check 6,000 lots: condos, lots outside the residential house zones, lots under an older bylaw, larger buildings and lots too irregular to measure. It also does not check heritage rules, trees, sewers or site-specific exceptions. This is a screening, not a permit or legal advice.

sections.heading: Questions to ask candidates
sections.template_text:
What, if anything, should the City do about its free multiplex designs on lots where they fit?
Should the City do more to tell residents what the multiplex rules allow on their street, and how?
The free designs are for detached lots. What should happen on streets where most homes are semis or row houses?
